parts:
Hi Jeryl,

the implementation of bincode() is indeed not available in 0.7.0-RC6, but in 0.7.0-RC7-SNAPSHOT. There is no stable release after 0.7.0-RC6 yet. You can find a list of releases of renjin-script-engine at http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/org/renjin/renjin-script-engine/.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan

cut <- function(x,cutpoints) {
    ret <- rep(1, length(x))

    for(i in cutpoints[-1]){
        i <- x > i
        ret[i] <- ret[i] + 1
    }

    ret

}

parts:
Hi Jeryl,

looking at your code, I'm wondering why you use the order() function in
x[['Tile']] <- ceiling( 5 * order(o) / length(o));

since o already contains the order of the elements in x. Also note that this implementation of ntile does not have the same behaviour as Oracle's NTILE() function where "The remainder values (the remainder of number of rows divided by buckets) are distributed one for each bucket, starting with bucket 1." (quoted from the Oracle docs)

If you are seeing different behavior between both versions of Renjin, can you provide us with a (fictitious) sample of x such that we can reproduce this issue?

Maarten-Jan
On Fri, Mar 7, 2014 at 7:26 PM, Jeryl Cook <jeryl...@vanity-soft.com> wrote:

Maarten,
I went back to using my orginal code that does not use 'cut'...but wanted to use the latest RC7 build....
However this snap shot breaks tests that use to work...

I have a simple R code that performs ntiles on  data.
x <- read.csv('myfile.csv', stringsAsFactors=FALSE);

o <- order(x[['ProcessCol']], x[['breakCol']] , decreasing=TRUE);

x[['Tile']] <- ceiling( 5 * order(o) / length(o));


in RC6 this is processing ntile correctly, however when i upgrade to use RC7-SNAPSHOT the data in 'Title' it produces is incorrect for the entire data set..

Hi Jeryl,

the implementation of bincode() is indeed not available in 0.7.0-RC6, but in 0.7.0-RC7-SNAPSHOT. There is no stable release after 0.7.0-RC6 yet. You can find a list of releases of renjin-script-engine at http://nexus.bedatadriven.com/content/groups/public/org/renjin/renjin-script-engine/.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan
